title: Pattaya 3 Days 2 Nights 2026 — Nong Nooch, Khao Chi Chan & Koh Larn | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: An unrushed 3-day, 2-night Pattaya itinerary in Thailand: day one Nong Nooch Garden with its elephant show plus Khao Chi Chan, day two a full beach day on Koh Larn, day three Pattaya viewpoints and food before heading home — with times, ticket prices, ferry schedules and real routes.

ogTitle: Pattaya 3 Days 2 Nights — Nong Nooch, Khao Chi Chan & Koh Larn
ogDesc: A real, doable 3-day, 2-night Pattaya plan: garden day, island day, food-and-souvenir day — with times, ticket prices, Koh Larn ferry schedule and where to eat.
intro: Three days and two nights is just the right length for Pattaya — you get the pretty gardens, an offshore island, and beachside food without running around all day. We've set up day one heading south to Nong Nooch Garden for the elephant show, then on to Khao Chi Chan to see the Buddha image carved into the cliff. Day two you take the ferry across to Koh Larn for a full day in the water, and on the last day you slowly pick off Pattaya's viewpoints, the local food, and a few souvenirs before heading back. Every stretch comes with times, realistic ballpark ticket prices, ferry schedules, and routes you can just follow.

blocks.html: Pattaya is easier to travel than a lot of people think — it's only about 2 hours from Bangkok, and you can drive yourself or take a van or bus without any hassle. But Pattaya town and places like Nong Nooch Garden and Khao Chi Chan are in different zones (those two sit south toward Sattahip, roughly 20–30 minutes from town). Plan the trip haphazardly and you'll waste time driving back and forth. So this 3-day, 2-night plan splits into three clear themes — a southern garden day, a full Koh Larn day, and a town-and-food day — so you're not doubling back.

blocks.title: Stay in one zone for both nights + sort out a car for day one
blocks.html: We'd suggest staying 2 nights in the same zone so you don't have to lug your bags around. If you're after quiet swimming with the family, stay on Jomtien Beach; if you'd rather walk to malls and food easily, stay in Central Pattaya. For day one heading south to Nong Nooch and Khao Chi Chan, if you're not driving yourself, hire a car with driver for the half day — it starts around 800–1,200 THB — or take a Grab to Nong Nooch and hire a car from there. The Koh Larn day has public ferries already, so you won't need a car.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Head south: Nong Nooch + Khao Chi Chan

blocks.html: Make the most of the single trip south on day one, because Nong Nooch Garden and Khao Chi Chan are close together near Sattahip — only about a 10–15 minute drive apart. Do Nong Nooch in the morning to early afternoon so you catch a show, then swing by Khao Chi Chan in the late afternoon when the sun softens. Two spots in one day, no rush.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Half a day at Nong Nooch · elephant show · Khao Chi Chan

items.activity: Leave your hotel and head south to Nong Nooch Garden (Sattahip)
items.note: From Pattaya town it's about a 20–30 minute drive south toward Sattahip. Nong Nooch is open 08:00–18:00 daily. Get there before noon and you'll have time to walk the garden before the sun gets harsh, and still catch a show.

items.activity: Walk the garden — French garden, dinosaur valley, photo spots
items.note: Adult entry is around 300 THB (garden only), or about 500 THB for the ticket that includes the show. It's huge inside; if you'd rather not walk so much there's a sightseeing tram for around 400 THB extra. The garden looks best in the morning before the sun bites — bring a hat and water.

items.activity: Watch the Thai cultural show and elephant show
items.note: There are several show times a day (around 10:30, 11:30, 13:30, 15:30) — double-check on site, as it can shift with the season. You'll see Thai dance, Muay Thai, and clever elephants. Use the combo ticket. You'll be done around midday.

items.activity: Lunch inside the garden, or eat at a spot around Sattahip
items.note: There's a food zone in the garden but at tourist prices. If you want to save, head out and eat wherever you like around central Sattahip or Na Jomtien. A simple meal runs about 120–250 THB per person.

items.activity: Drive on to Khao Chi Chan (about 10–15 minutes)
items.note: Khao Chi Chan is in Na Jomtien, Sattahip district, close to Nong Nooch. It's open 08:00–18:00 and currently free to enter. It's a line-drawn Buddha image carved into a cliff face nearly 100 metres tall — you can see it clearly from far off.

items.activity: Pay respects, photograph the wide plaza below the cliff, stroll the grounds
items.note: The open plaza in front of the Buddha is good for low-angle shots that capture the whole image. Dress modestly. By late afternoon the sun has eased and it's pleasant to walk around — figure about 40–60 minutes.

items.activity: Head back into town, rest at the hotel, recharge
items.note: It's about a 30-minute drive back into Pattaya town. Rest for a bit before heading out for dinner. You've done a lot of walking around the garden today, so take it easy.

items.activity: Seafood dinner by the sea, or a spot in town
items.note: Pattaya has plenty of seafood places, both around Naklua and along Jomtien Beach. Pick one with clearly posted prices that locals go to. Seafood is priced by weight, around 350–700 THB per person. If you want something lighter, there are made-to-order Thai spots all over town.

blocks.title: Check show times and the rainy season before you go
blocks.html: The elephant and cultural show times at Nong Nooch can shift with festivals and how busy it is — calling or checking the website before your trip is the safer bet. Khao Chi Chan is an open-air plaza, so if you're coming in the rainy season (May–Oct), bring an umbrella and aim for a gap between showers.

blocks.text: Day 2 — A full day on Koh Larn, swim till you drop

blocks.html: Today is the highlight of the trip. Take the ferry from Bali Hai Pier across to Koh Larn, the island just off Pattaya where the water is far clearer than the beaches in town. There are several beaches to choose from: Tawaen Beach is busy with lots of activities, while Samae Beach and Nuan Beach are quieter and better for lazing about. Go in the morning and come back in the evening — you can do a full day without needing to stay overnight.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Ferry to the island · swim · eat seafood on the island

items.activity: Head to Bali Hai Pier and buy a ferry ticket to the island
items.note: Bali Hai Pier is at the far end of South Pattaya Road. The regular passenger ferry costs around 30 THB per person and takes about 30–45 minutes. Ferries run on a schedule (morning runs are often 07:00, 08:00, 09:00 depending on which beach you're heading to). Check the latest return times at the pier before you cross over.

items.activity: Arrive on Koh Larn, pick your beach
items.note: Tawaen Beach is the main one, with umbrellas and loungers to rent and the full range of water activities. If you want quiet, take a songthaew on the island over to Samae, Nuan, or Tien Beach. Songthaews on the island run about 20–40 THB per person per ride.

items.activity: Swim, rent a lounger and umbrella, or do a water activity
items.note: A lounger plus umbrella rents for around 100–200 THB. The water is clear and easy to swim in. Add-on activities like jet ski, parasailing, and banana boat are priced separately — always agree on the price and photograph the condition of the gear before you use it, to avoid being charged for damage later.

items.activity: Lunch — seafood or made-to-order on the island
items.note: Restaurants on the island serve seafood, som tam, and fried rice, a touch pricier than the mainland because of shipping costs, around 150–350 THB per person. Check the price board before ordering, especially for seafood that's priced by weight.

items.activity: Rest under the umbrella, take photos, stroll along the beach
items.note: The afternoon sun is strong, so rest under the umbrella and reapply sunscreen. Koh Larn's clear water is great for photos, and the hilltop viewpoints above some beaches are lovely too — if you have time, take a songthaew up.

items.activity: Pack up and catch an afternoon ferry back to the mainland
items.note: Check the return ferry times carefully. Afternoon–evening runs usually go until around 17:00–18:00, but don't wait for the very last one — it gets packed, and if you miss it you'll have to charter a speedboat, which is pricier (from around 150 THB per person). Allow yourself an extra 20–30 minutes to get to the pier.

items.activity: Back in Pattaya, rest, then find dinner
items.note: You'll be tired from the sun and sea today, so keep dinner easy and close to your hotel. If you fancy a night market, save it for tomorrow.

blocks.title: Always check the weather before boarding the ferry
blocks.html: The Koh Larn ferries depend on the wind and waves. If the sea is rough or there's a storm, ferries may be cancelled or delayed, especially during the monsoon (roughly May–Oct). Check the forecast and ask at the pier before you go. If you get seasick, take medication before boarding, and keep an eye on kids and valuables on the crowded ferry.

items.activity: Easy breakfast near your hotel, then pack and check out
items.note: Check out first and leave your bags at the hotel so you can sightsee without dragging them around. Breakfast of congee, rice soup, or coffee at a nearby spot runs about 60–120 THB per person.

items.activity: Pratumnak Hill Viewpoint (Pattaya Viewpoint)
items.note: A popular viewpoint on Pratumnak Hill, where you can fit the whole curve of Pattaya Bay in one frame. There's a Pattaya City sign for photos, and no entry fee. Mid-morning the sun isn't harsh yet and it's not too crowded.

items.activity: Stop at a seaside café, or visit Wat Khao Phra Yai
items.note: There are several seaside cafés near the viewpoint, drinks around 90–160 THB. Or stop by Wat Khao Phra Yai (Big Buddha Hill) to pay respects at the large hilltop Buddha — open morning to evening, no entry fee, dress modestly.

items.activity: Lunch — noodles or made-to-order at a well-known spot in town
items.note: Pattaya town has lots of punchy Thai places; pick one where locals queue. An easy lunch runs about 80–200 THB per person before you go souvenir shopping.

items.activity: Buy souvenirs — Lan Pho Naklua Market or a souvenir shop in town
items.note: Lan Pho Naklua Market is the go-to for dried seafood and sea souvenirs — dried shrimp, squid, chilli pastes. Pick a stall locals shop at where things are fresh and clean; you can haggle a little.

items.activity: Grab your bags from the hotel, then head home
items.note: Come back for your bags. If you're taking a van or bus back to Bangkok there are several departure points in town; the trip takes about 2 hours. Allow extra time for traffic on holiday evenings.

blocks.html: If you arrive in Pattaya early on the first day and want a night out, you can swap day three's plan and do the night market or Walking Street the evening before — whatever's easier. Reorder things to fit your transport and flight times; this plan is a framework you can shift around.

blocks.text: Pattaya food you shouldn't skip on the trip

items.name: Fresh seafood (Naklua / Jomtien beachfront)
items.blurb: Shrimp, shellfish, crab, fish — pick what's fresh, have it weighed, then ordered cooked. Crab in curry powder, grilled prawns, blanched cockles — this is the main event for most people who come to Pattaya. Pick a place with clearly posted prices that locals go to.

items.name: Boat noodles / tom yum noodles, Pattaya
items.blurb: Punchy central-Thai-style noodles served in small bowls so you can have several. A few long-running spots in town are well known — a light meal to slot in during the day.

items.name: Som tam, grilled chicken, sticky rice
items.blurb: The classic beach combo — order it under an umbrella by the sea or at a shop in town. Bold and fully seasoned, it suits Pattaya's heat.

items.name: Seafood on Koh Larn
items.blurb: Grilled squid, grilled prawns, crab fried rice — eaten over clear-water sea views on the island. A touch pricier than the mainland because of shipping, so check the price board before ordering.

items.name: Night-market street food
items.blurb: Grilled pork skewers, grilled meatballs, roti, fried snacks, desserts — wander and graze in the evening around the night markets and Walking Street. Easy on the wallet.

items.name: Seaside cafés
items.blurb: Coffee, tea, cake, and a sea breeze. Around Jomtien and Pratumnak there are several cafés with sea views — a good place to take a break between sightseeing.

items.name: Dried seafood (Naklua souvenirs)
items.blurb: Dried shrimp, dried squid, roasted chilli paste — the classic Pattaya souvenirs. Buy them at Lan Pho Naklua Market; pick a stall locals shop at.

items.name: International food in town
items.blurb: Pattaya has plenty of international restaurants — Japanese, Korean, Indian, Western — for the day you want a break from seafood. Prices span several tiers.

blocks.text: Rough budget per person (3 days, 2 nights)

items: Accommodation, 2 nights — a mid-range hotel in town/Jomtien at 700–1,800 THB/night (split between 2 people) works out to about 700–1,800 THB/person · prices climb on long weekends and in high season
Nong Nooch — garden-only ticket around 300 THB, combo ticket with show around 500 THB, sightseeing tram add-on around 400 THB (children discounted)
Koh Larn — ferry round trip around 60 THB + island songthaews + lounger and umbrella 100–200 THB, totalling around 200–400 THB (water activities not included)
Khao Chi Chan — free entry, no charge
Food — 7–8 meals, around 1,200–2,500 THB for the whole trip, depending on whether you go for seafood or street food
Getting around locally — town songthaews from 10–30 THB/ride, a hired car on day one 800–1,200 THB, or Grab in stretches
Rough total — around 3,500–6,500 THB/person, not including travel from Bangkok

blocks.text: Enjoy Pattaya with peace of mind — things to watch

items: Nightlife districts — Pattaya has lively night zones like Walking Street. You can go out, but keep your wits about you, watch your valuables, wallet, and phone, don't drink past the point of control, and be wary of touts pulling you into venues and padded bills that can run far too high. Always ask the price first.

Water activities — for jet skis and parasailing, agree on the price and photograph or film the condition of the gear before using it, to guard against being charged for damage later, which has been a known problem in Pattaya.
Island ferries — check the weather before boarding, wear a life jacket if one's provided, keep kids close, and remember ferries may be suspended during the monsoon.
Prices swing with season and holidays — rooms and tours go up on long weekends and in high season (Nov–Feb). Book ahead and compare a few places.
Seafood priced by weight — check the per-kilo price board, have it weighed in front of you, and ask for the total before ordering, especially pricey items like lobster and crab.

faq.q: Is 3 days and 2 nights enough for Pattaya?
faq.a: It's enough and just about right. Split it into a day heading south to Nong Nooch for the elephant show and on to Khao Chi Chan, a full day on Koh Larn by ferry, and a day picking off Pattaya's viewpoints plus food and souvenirs before you leave. You get the gardens, an offshore island, and beachside food without running around all day.

faq.q: How much is Nong Nooch entry, and what time is the elephant show?
faq.a: Garden-only adult entry is around 300 THB, and the combo ticket with the cultural and elephant shows is around 500 THB (children discounted). There's a sightseeing tram add-on for around 400 THB. The garden is open 08:00–18:00, and the shows run several times a day (around 10:30, 11:30, 13:30, 15:30). We'd suggest checking the latest times on site, as they can shift with the season.

faq.q: Where do you catch the Koh Larn ferry, how much is it, and how long does it take?
faq.a: You take the ferry from Bali Hai Pier at the end of South Pattaya Road. The regular passenger ferry costs around 30 THB per person and takes about 30–45 minutes, with runs starting in the morning around 07:00. If you want to be faster, there are speedboats from around 150 THB per person that take about 10–15 minutes. Check the return times and the weather at the pier before you cross over.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for Khao Chi Chan, and how far is it from Pattaya town?
faq.a: Khao Chi Chan is free to enter, no charge. It's in Na Jomtien, Sattahip district, about 30 minutes south of Pattaya town, and only about 10–15 minutes from Nong Nooch — so the two are easy to do in one day. It's open 08:00–18:00 daily.

faq.q: Can you do this plan without driving yourself?
faq.a: Yes. The Koh Larn day has public ferries already, so no car needed. For day one heading south to Nong Nooch and Khao Chi Chan, which are both out of town, we'd suggest hiring a car with driver for the half day, starting around 800–1,200 THB, or taking a Grab and hiring a car from there. In town you can use the beach-route songthaews, from 10–30 THB per ride.
